what: Periphery symmetry of the official SBI recipe (mapooon/SelfBlendedImages)

A_parameter_sharing.note: Identical inputs to `image` and `image1`. 0 means albumentations replays one parameter set across targets, so the JPEG quality is the same for fake and real.

B_periphery_symmetry.note: after_blend=0 confirms dynamic_blend composites onto the array returned as the real. A nonzero value after the shared transforms is JPEG non-locality, not asymmetry -- test C localizes it.

C_spatial_extent.note: Compression forced on (p=1) to bound the worst case. periphery_blocks() dilates the mask by 24 px, so every band below that is excluded from the T1 audit anyway.

verdict: NO LEAK in the official recipe: parameters are shared across targets, the blend composites onto the array returned as the real, and any residual difference dies within one 8x8 JPEG block (max 0.0 beyond 8 px) -- inside the 24px dilation the audit already discards. The official pipeline would score the null 0.500 in T1. Finding 1 is therefore a defect in OUR self_blend, not a property of SBI: we composite onto a separately-perturbed copy (deviation 1) and re-encode the blend only (deviation 2).
